articleTitle: Network management for a public land mobile network
publicationTitle: IEE Colloquium on Network Management for Personal and Mobile Telecommunications Systems (Digest No. 1994/195)
abstract: In the search for a computer based solution to support all processes needed to run a large public land mobile network (PLMN), the D1 network operator DeTeMobil, has decided to implement a family of management systems according to international network management standards. The result is an operating support system for the D1-PLMN (D1-OSS) based on network mangement functionalities according to ISO 10165 and contains the following: fault management; configuration management; performance mangement; accounting management; and security management. The implementation is based on the principles outlined in CCITT M.3010 recommendation.

articleTitle: Determination of network performance by the analysis of burst error activity
publicationTitle: IEE Colloquium on Network Management for Personal and Mobile Telecommunications Systems (Digest No. 1994/195)
abstract: Network operators and manufacturers are continually striving to improve the quality of service provided by networks. Mobile networks also have the additional problems of time and connection variant performance. In order to establish and improve the quality of service being offered to customers a mechanism is required to reliably and accurately determine the performance of the network. This paper briefly reviews the present mechanisms and describes a new mechanism based on metrics of error burst power spectral density.

articleTitle: Multivendor possibilities in GSM radio networks
publicationTitle: IEE Colloquium on Network Management for Personal and Mobile Telecommunications Systems (Digest No. 1994/195)
abstract: In general, a multivendor environment offers advantages for both network operators and manufacturers. For a network operator, the multivendor environment introduces competition in investments and independence from one supplier. For a manufacturer multivendor environment offers a possibility to be the second supplier in an existing network. In a GSM network, the most interesting part from the multivendor point of view is the radio network where most of the investments are made. The GSM's telecommunications specifications support a multivendor environment and most of the existing implementations are interoperable from this point of view. However, the network management specifications are still to be finalised. The problems and possibilities of introducing a multivendor environment regarding network management are presented for the following cases: multiple vendors at the base station system (BSS) level; and multiple vendors at the base station (BTS) level.

articleTitle: Challenges of specifying and implementing a Q3 network management interface in a GSM network
publicationTitle: IEE Colloquium on Network Management for Personal and Mobile Telecommunications Systems (Digest No. 1994/195)
abstract: The telecommunications management network (TMN) philosophy for management of modern complex telecommunications systems specifies the use of a Q3 interface based on open systems interconnection (OSI) standards, for exchange of network management information. The paper focuses on the challenges of implementing Q3 technology for the GSM system. Simplification of the day to day operation of their network has led many operators to look for a network management solution that can integrate all their diverse equipment and allow them to take advantage of the economic benefits of GSM technology. This will generally result in the operator selecting a centralised management system to coordinate the activities of the various subsystems. The key to being able to integrate the operations and maintenance (O&M) activities is the availability of suitable interfaces for the exchange of management information between the different systems.

articleTitle: Management of a trunked mobile communication system using the open Cogsys real-time applications and expert system environment
publicationTitle: IEE Colloquium on Network Management for Personal and Mobile Telecommunications Systems (Digest No. 1994/195)
abstract: Describes the result of a joint software development project undertaken by British Gas Telecomms Services and Cogsys Ltd. The purpose of the development was to create a computer based management system for a trunked private mobile radio system which British Gas operate in the North West of England.

articleTitle: Components, modelling and robustness of network management for telecommunications systems
publicationTitle: IEE Colloquium on Network Management for Personal and Mobile Telecommunications Systems (Digest No. 1994/195)
abstract: Analog cellular technology using frequency reuse has advantages of coverage, speech quality and initial costs (radio vs, fixed infrastructure) and disadvantage of interference. Many people depend on telecommunication networks and telecommunication network management allows their objectives to be met. The system management model manages resources remotely using agents which can be notified by the managed objects. The principles of knowledge based network management, configuration management, and fault management and security are discussed.

articleTitle: Functions for managing the network-an operational perspective
publicationTitle: IEE Colloquium on Network Management for Personal and Mobile Telecommunications Systems (Digest No. 1994/195)
abstract: In the design of a mobile network, the initial attention is normally focused on technical functions of base stations, switches, microwave, cross connects etc. and the difficulties in acquiring sites and set-up of the equipment. Network management functions of the equipment has often no or only little weight during the contract negotiations. These functions get more attention during the day to day work in an operational network. Each equipment is usually delivered with its own operation and maintenance centre. This leads to the effect that in the operational centres a lot of different machines are installed. Due to the vital importance of intelligent network management to the availability, quality and the commercial success of a mobile network, consideration should be given from the very beginning to integrate these systems and functions into the planning process. The paper describes various functions for managing the network from an operational perspective. It gives the purpose of each function and a brief outline of interfaces and working methods involved.
